ellie.cs: Heads-up — ticket #7893 from Gridline. They deprovisioned ~12 users in Okta yesterday but those accounts still show as active in Redwood and retain org roles. Customer says Okta rotated their SCIM token at ~2025-10-02T09:05:00Z. Can we triage?

maya.solutions: Thanks Ellie. Do we have the SCIM audit logs from their tenant? Any 4xx/5xx spikes around the token rotation time?

ellie.cs: Pasting trimmed log (anonymized):
```
2025-10-02T09:11:48Z PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00ab12 - 403 {
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "error_description": "token missing required scope: groups.write"
}
2025-10-02T09:11:49Z PATCH /scim/v2/Users/01234 - 200
2025-10-02T09:11:50Z PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00ab12 - 401 {"error":"invalid_token"}
2025-10-02T09:12:03Z GET /scim/v2/Groups/00ab12 - 200 (members returned without externalId fields)
```

ellie.cs: They also attached the Okta SCIM connector logs saying the admin rotated keys at 09:05 and retried a bulk group update.

ana.engineer: I can look. Quick read: two things jump out — (1) the token used for the group PATCH lacked groups.write scope so our groups write path rejected removal of members, (2) later calls returned 200 but with members lacking externalId which breaks our membership reconcile (we rely on externalId to map Okta member -> Redwood user id). When externalId is missing we try a best-effort match by email, which in some cases results in no-op and roles stay.

ana.engineer: From the runtime perspective, our SCIM handler has this guard: we only accept removals when we can identify members by externalId or by userId. If the incoming PATCH uses "members" that are only {display: "Alice"} we won't remove their role mapping because the deletion path is ambiguous.

jim.prod: Is this a new failure mode or an edge case? We should assess impact (how many orgs) and whether to ship a hotfix or provide a customer remediation doc.

ana.engineer: Edge-case but actionable. Two remediation paths:
1) Customer-level: ask Gridline to re-issue a SCIM token with full required scopes (users.write, groups.write, members.write) and trigger a full group resync. That should allow our service to remove memberships correctly.
2) Server-side: implement a conservative fallback where if a Group PATCH comes in with member objects missing externalId but there is a preceding 401/403 token rotation window, we queue a follow-up reconciliation job that fetches group members and resolves externalIds via email/username and then applies removals. This reduces manual work but needs careful safety checks.

scim-bot: automated-alert: provisioning-failure-rate spike detected for Gridline tenant between 2025-10-02T09:10 and 09:20 UTC — 42 failures (majority 403 insufficient_scope).

maya.solutions: For immediate customer unblock, Ellie — can you request Gridline to re-issue the connector token with the full SCIM scopes (I'll paste the exact list)? Also ask them to run a full group push/resync after token swap. I can run a manual cleanup if needed.

ellie.cs: On it. What's the exact scope set to request?

ana.engineer: Ask for: "scim.users.write scim.users.read scim.groups.write scim.groups.read scim.members.write" (exact wording in the docs). And ask them not to do a mid-update token rotation while a bulk push is running; if they must rotate, pause pushes for ~5m.

jim.prod: For product follow-up: create a short RFC for the reconciliation fallback and an operator tool to scan orgs for "orphaned roles" (users with roles assigned but not present in any active group membership) so Support can triage quickly.

ellie.cs: Gridline confirmed they rotated the token and immediately retried a bulk group update. They're happy to re-issue the token and run a resync. I'll coordinate and report back.

ana.engineer: I'll draft a small script to scan the org for orphaned roles and to safely remove role bindings when the user is no longer in any group. It will log deletions and require a manual confirmation flag for production runs.

maya.solutions: Perfect — once we have the script we can offer a one-time free cleanup for Gridline.

ellie.cs: Action items:
- ellie.cs: get Gridline to re-issue token + run resync (in progress)
- ana.engineer: prototype reconciliation/job + orphaned-role cleanup script (ETA today EOD)
- jim.prod: RFC for fallback behavior + operator scan (ETA 2 days)
- maya.solutions: standby to run manual cleanup and notify customer communications

ellie.cs: tagging for visibility @ana.engineer @jim.prod @maya.solutions :thumbsup: 

maya.solutions: thanks — will follow up with Gridline once ana posts the script.

ellie.cs: closing loop here after cleanup. Will post final status in this thread.
